title: Pull requests, CI checks, and controlled deployment
summary: Prepare a reviewable change with truthful validation, metadata dependencies, explicit target environment, and recovery steps.
prerequisites: M28 Git state and focused changes.
Setup guide deployment and M10/M24 tests.
learningObjectives: Distinguish repository checks, org validation, deployment, and smoke testing.
Plan recovery beyond reverting source files.

sections.heading: Understand the mechanism
body: A pull request is a review boundary: it presents a proposed change, its reason, and evidence that helps another person assess it. A useful description begins with a concrete trigger and resulting behavior. For Northstar, 'repeated warranty submissions now return the existing request' is more informative than a list of files or a claim that the integration was improved.

Continuous integration runs repeatable checks when code changes. Formatting, static analysis, local JavaScript tests, and metadata structure checks can run without a Salesforce org. Apex execution and deployment validation require an appropriate org and authentication. State which checks actually ran. A green repository workflow does not mean Apex passed if no org was connected.

A deployment plan includes the complete dependency set: custom fields, objects, permission sets, classes, Flow versions, configuration records, and any post-deploy activation or data preparation. Credentials require secure provisioning outside source code. Validate the selected package against the intended environment and make the target explicit; a default alias is not a sufficient safeguard against using the wrong org.

Review, validation, deployment, and smoke testing answer different questions. Review examines design and risks; validation checks deployability and selected tests; deployment changes the target; smoke testing verifies a small real user path afterward. The recovery plan must distinguish code rollback from data repair and external effects. Reverting a commit does not cancel a request already sent to another system.

callouts.text: Each green check proves a particular property; name that property and do not claim more.

sections.heading: Northstar Motors worked example
body: Prepare a PR for the M18 duplicate-request correction. Include the unique key field if it is new, the service changes, tests, and any permission changes. Describe the before/after case: the same key delivered three times previously created repeated work; now it returns one existing request, while conflicting payload reuse is rejected.

Your release checklist should identify a target training org, expected validation command, required secret provisioning, activation order, and one restricted-user smoke test. If only local checks are available, mark org validation Not run rather than fabricating a passed result. This still creates a reviewable artifact and clearly identifies the remaining gate.

callouts.text: Which evidence proves the restricted user can use the deployed feature, rather than merely that the metadata parsed?

codeBlocks.caption: Review evidence checklist, not an automatically executed pipeline
codeBlocks.code:
Change: repeated WARRANTY-100 returns the existing request
Local checks: command + observed result
Apex tests: org alias + test names + observed result, or Not run
Dependencies: object/field/permission/Flow configuration
Deploy target: explicitly named training org
Smoke test: restricted user + repeat request + expected record count
Recovery: source rollback, data repair, and external-effect handling

sections.heading: Build and inspect
body: Use a PR inside your personal training repository or the approved submission workflow. Do not put Salesforce tokens in the PR, repository files, screenshots, or untrusted pull-request workflow environments.

steps.title: Create a focused PR
steps.instruction: Inspect the complete diff and remove unrelated metadata. Write the problem, behavior, validation, dependencies, and limitations.
steps.expected: A reviewer can understand the change without reading the entire chat history.

steps.title: Run appropriate checks
steps.instruction: Execute available local tests and, when an authorized training org is connected, the selected org validation/tests. Record commands, target, and actual outcome.
steps.expected: Every reported result is tied to a real execution.

steps.title: Plan deployment and recovery
steps.instruction: Order schema, code, permissions, activation, and data preparation as needed. Define stop conditions and a post-deploy user smoke test.
steps.expected: The plan covers failure after deployment as well as before it.

sections.heading: Failure cases and boundaries
body: A CI workflow that exposes deployment credentials to untrusted code can turn review into an unintended privileged operation. Keep validation identities and execution boundaries deliberate.
A successful deploy can still leave a Flow inactive or a user without a needed permission. These post-deploy conditions belong in the checklist and smoke test.

callouts.text: Do not equate a reverted Git commit with reversal of data migrations or external side effects.

exercise.title: Prepare a reviewable release
exercise.brief: Create a focused PR and release checklist for one completed Middle feature.
steps: Attach actual check results and dependencies.
Write deployment, smoke, and recovery steps.
acceptance: No check is marked passed without evidence.
Target org and permissions are explicit.
Recovery includes data and external effects where relevant.
exercise.stretch: Explain one limitation and propose a small follow-up experiment before extending the implementation.

knowledgeCheck.question: What does a local Jest pass prove?
knowledgeCheck.answer: The mocked component behavior covered by those tests, not live Apex or org permissions.

knowledgeCheck.question: Why list metadata dependencies?
knowledgeCheck.answer: A class or Flow may work in the development org only because undeclared fields or configuration already exist there.

knowledgeCheck.question: What may require forward repair?
knowledgeCheck.answer: Data changes or external actions that a source rollback cannot automatically undo.
